title: test(server): synchronize cold-client cancellation after initializer ownership handoff
body:
## Observed failure

PR #152 at `fb772551cff6b4620a6fcdb94c57b78350cebb33` initially failed the unchanged test `project_session::tests::p5d_cancelled_cold_client_keeps_initializer_fenced_until_publication` in P7 closeout run [37744918344, attempt 1](https://github.com/jyqj/codecortex/actions/runs/37744918344/attempts/1). The assertion at `project_session.rs:620` inferred worker ownership from `live_projects.try_lock().is_err()`.

A deterministic control using the locked Tokio 1.50 dependency demonstrates that an owned-lock future can be queued, reserve the semaphore permit after the current holder drops, and make `try_lock()` fail **before that future is repolled and before any worker starts**. Dropping that unpolled waiter then releases the permit. The existing predicate therefore does not establish that the initializer has received the owned guard.

The original test passed unchanged locally at the same source; one bounded failed-jobs rerun passed. All three exact-head workflows passed before #152 was merged as `804e56fe1cb2e1e2b7b9a1e879f84bda048c0a1b`. Preserve the first failure in the audit trail. These observations identify a test synchronization flaw; they do not prove every product cancellation path.

## Required follow-up

Use a deterministic test hook/barrier that confirms the blocking initializer actually owns the guard before cancelling its client. Keep the original production requirement and assertion: an active initializer must retain the cold guard until publication. Cover cancellation before handoff separately. Do not use sleeps, repeated reruns, or weakened assertions as the repair.

## Existing evidence

- First-failure log SHA-256: `79c5b16517ec7ab21f16a057849f8e69ef0e8c2ee5dbf627eebfd35587babd88`.
- Deterministic reservation-control receipt SHA-256: `d6ba09036d4fbbb4aec20b386b984102b89fa23a52ea28e82ceecb127a9ab357`.
- Exact-head terminal CI receipt SHA-256: `b4ad1e465d19e936a343e02bb1ebb77a308a2584c758590fa6ca4853154578bd`.

This is a follow-up from PR management, not an additional completed item in the original 192-task roadmap.
